q: A student listens to two professional recordings of the same piece, one orchestral and one for band, and notes similarities and differences. What is she doing?
o: Comparing and contrasting exemplary musical examples

q: Which listening task best compares two live performances?
o: Noting differences in tone, balance and interpretation

q: A singer reads a melody in solfège, then compares it with the harmony part sung by another section. What is she comparing?
Which part usually carries the main tune in a choral piece?
e: The melody is the featured line.

q: The interval from C up to G is a ___.
e: C to G spans five letter names.

q: A minor triad differs from a major triad because its third is what?
e: Minor chords have a minor third.

q: Compare 3/4 and 6/8. What is a key difference?
o: 3/4 is simple meter and 6/8 is compound meter
e: Simple meters divide the beat in two; compound in three.

q: A student counts 1-la-li, 2-la-li in a measure. This is a counting system for which meter?
e: Three subdivisions per beat signal compound meter.

q: A song that follows A-B-A-C-A form is a ___.
e: A rondo returns to the A theme between contrasting sections.

q: Binary form has how many main sections?
Hearing the trumpets cover the clarinets in a band piece is a problem of what?
e: Balance is the relative volume of parts.

q: When all voices in a choir sound as one unified tone, they have achieved good ___.
e: Blend is unity of tone color.

q: Comparing a march and a waltz mainly contrasts which element?
e: Marches and waltzes use different meters.

q: The overall pitch center around which a piece is organized is its what?
What helps prevent vocal strain during a long rehearsal?
o: Drinking water and resting the voice when needed
e: Hydration and rest protect the voice.

q: A brass player feels tension in her shoulders. Which adjustment is best?
o: Relax the shoulders and check posture

q: A measure in 6/8 time may contain which grouping of eighth notes?
e: 6/8 is typically felt in two beats.

q: A student writes a rhythm using an asymmetrical pattern of 2+2+3. Which meter is it?
What does allegro tell a performer?
o: Play at a fast, lively tempo

q: A line above a note telling the player to stress and sustain it is called what?
A player who keeps her tone full, focused and in style as pieces grow harder is showing what?
What most improves a flutist's tone color?
o: Steady air support and a stable embouchure

q: Which posture best supports a seated clarinetist's breathing?

Which habit causes uneven rhythm?
A piece has three flats in the key signature. Which notes are flatted?
e: The order of flats is B, E, A, D, G.

q: When a piece changes from major to minor mode, what usually changes?
o: Some scale degrees are lowered and the mood darkens

q: A trombonist adjusts her slide to match the section's pitch. She is working on what?
Where should a singer breathe in a phrase?
o: At punctuation or musical rests where the sense allows

q: A student composes a short piece for her own instrument within her technical ability. This reflects what?
o: Creating music at an appropriate level of difficulty

q: Why record an original phrase after writing it?
o: To hear it and evaluate whether it works

q: A sight reader keeps a warm, controlled tone even on an unfamiliar piece. This shows what?
o: Increasingly mature sound while sight reading

q: Which step helps maintain tone while sight reading?
o: Breathing deeply and keeping a relaxed embouchure

q: A cellist sight reads while keeping her left hand relaxed and bow arm balanced. She is applying what?
Sight reading with tension in the neck will most likely cause what?
While sight reading, a student scans for slurs and accents before starting. She is preparing what?
Which method helps count a tricky rhythm in sight reading?
o: Speaking syllables such as 1 e & a

q: A piece modulates from G major to D major. What should a sight reader watch for?
o: A new key signature or added accidentals

q: When mode changes from major to minor mid-piece, a sight reader should do what?
o: Adjust to the new accidentals and tonal center

q: Before singing a new melody, a student labels the first notes with numbers 1-3-5. She is using what?
Which is a melodic reading system?
A sight reader follows crescendo markings and shapes phrases while reading. She is applying what?
What should a sight reader do at a phrase marking?
o: Shape the line with direction and a natural release

q: A singer uses tall, rounded vowels so a chord rings in tune while sight reading. She is working on what?
Listening to the bass line helps the ensemble tune because the bass provides what?

Which pair of styles differs mainly in culture of origin?
A marching band performing at a football game shows music used for what?
National anthems are an example of music used to express what?
Studying the physics of vibrating strings connects music with what subject?
Setting a poem to music connects music with what subject?

Using software to correct pitch in a recording shows how technology affects what?
Using someone else's recording in a video without permission raises what concern?

o: Tools for college and career preparation

q: Which is a useful college-prep tool for a musician?
As an audience member at a recital, you should do what?
o: Silence your phone and stay quiet during the music

q: As a performer, what shows concert etiquette?
o: Bowing or acknowledging applause with courtesy

q: A class writes criteria for judging balance, blend and intonation in a choir performance. This is what?
Which evaluation applies criteria well?
o: The altos blended nicely but the tempo dragged in the second verse

q: A student sets monthly goals and checks them against recordings of her playing. She is using what?
Which tool supports personal artistic improvement?
A student listens to a professional recording and compares her section's blend to it. She is doing what?
o: Evaluating performance against an exemplary model

q: After comparing to an exemplary model, what is a good next step?
o: Set a specific goal and rehearse it
